newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end mixed, crush pace lifts August.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end mixed, crush pace lifts August.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended mixed on Friday with August up on a larger than expected weekly crush figure and new crop down slightly amid conflicting weather forecasts, traders said.
"The crush was much better than expected and Dreyfus is taking beans out of the Lakes, so it's not a surprise August is strong," a trader said.

The weekly National Oilseeds Processors Association crush report early Friday showed the U.S. soybean crush during the week ended July 23 at 23.891 million bushels, at the high end of expectations of 20.25 million to 24.0 million bushels.
Soybeans ended 2-1/2 cents per bushel higher to 1/2 cent lower with August up 2-1/2 at $7.54-1/2.
Bull spreads were active on the day, tied to ideas of demand for nearby supplies and expectations for a bumper new crop, traders said.
Traders pointed to news that Taiwan bought 108,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans, double the amount they had tendered for.

New crop months ended a choppy session a shade lower. Traders cited uncertainties over weather forecasts. Forecasts called for a hot weekend, followed by a cool down and chances for showers, but meteorologists disagreed on rainfall amounts.
Some forecasters suggested widespread coverage across the southern half of the Corn Belt while others expected closer to 50 percent coverage.
The trade has been fixating on forecasts for dry weather. Traders said after a hot weekend, rainfall will be vital to crop development.

Spreads were the key play for a second day. Pit sources said Continental Grain bull spread two million bushels August/November at $1.54 to $1.56, premium August. Cargill Investor Services, Tenco Inc, Farmers Commodities Corp, Iowa Grain and Payne Webber were also said to be bull spreaders.
Tenco also bought 1.5 million August outright and FIMAT Futures, Refco Inc and Prudential Securities each bought one million November.
Iowa Grain sold 2.5 million November and ING sold 1.5 million November.
In options trade, Tenco bought 400 September $6.50 calls at 21 cents and Louis Dreyfus sold 200 September $6.75 calls and 200 September $6.50 puts at 26 to 27 cents.
Volatility in the November closed at 21-1/2 percent, down from 22 percent on Thursday.

Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 48,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 34,624 contracts. Options volume was pegged at 13,000 contracts, against Wednesday's 12,903.
